content_units: You already have a good base for networking and Windows admin, so this plan shifts more time toward   cryptography, governance, risk, and compliance   while keeping hands-on practice steady. With   10.5 hours/week   available, the schedule is enough for a solid first-attempt pass if you stay consistent and start practice questions early.
Week   Dates   Focus   Key Sessions   Goal/Quiz

1   Week 1   Exam setup; Domain map; Threats overview   Weekdays: exam objectives + threat actors/malware/social engineering; Sat: baseline 60-question diagnostic + review   Build study tracker; identify weak areas

2   Week 2   Security architecture; secure design; enterprise infrastructure   Weekdays: network segmentation, cloud models, zero trust, resilience; Sat: mixed quiz + notes cleanup   Be able to explain major architecture concepts

3   Week 3   Cryptography foundations   Weekdays: symmetric vs asymmetric, hashing, PKI, certs, key exchange, digital signatures; Sat: crypto-focused drill set   Remove confusion around core crypto terms

4   Week 4   Cryptography applied; PKI and secure protocols   Weekdays: TLS, IPsec, SSH, VPNs, wireless security, certificates in practice; Sat: scenario questions + flashcards   Answer protocol/certificate questions confidently
5   Week 5   Identity and access management   Weekdays: AAA, federation, SSO, MFA, RBAC/ABAC, PAM; Sat: timed mixed quiz   Strengthen access-control and auth design knowledge

6   Week 6   Governance, risk, compliance   Weekdays: policies, standards, procedures, risk types, BCP/DR, audits, privacy, training; Sat: governance-heavy quiz + summary sheet   Turn weak governance area into a reliable scoring domain

7   Week 7   Security operations and incident response   Weekdays: logging, monitoring, alerting, forensics basics, playbooks, vulnerability management; Sat: PBQ-style walkthroughs   Improve response workflow and operations vocabulary

8   Week 8   Program management; review weak domains   Weekdays: secure change management, third-party risk, data lifecycle, mixed review; Sat: full-length timed practice exam   Reach passing range on practice test
9   Week 9   Intensive revision and exam-style execution   Weekdays: 30-40 mixed questions/day + targeted review; Sat: second full-length practice exam + error log   Stabilize performance and timing
10   Week 10   Final polish and exam readiness   Weekdays: flashcards, missed concepts, light drills; Sat: short confidence review only, no cramming   Walk into exam rested and consistent
Weekly Rhythm That Fits a Full-Time Job
Use the same structure Monday through Friday to reduce friction:
-   35 min  : take notes and map concepts to exam objectives
-   25 min  : practice questions on that topic
-   90 min  : timed quiz or practice exam block
-   30 min  : build/update condensed notes or flashcards
Option 1: Official exam objectives + one primary video course   Use as the backbone for coverage and pacing     Highest priority
Option 2: One good practice-test bank   Best ROI for score improvement and timing     Must buy
Option 3: One concise Security+ study guide   Best for governance, acronyms, and structured review     High value
Option 4: Flashcard app / self-made cards   Best for crypto, ports, controls, governance terms     Low cost
Target total:   about   USD 80-140  , leaving room for one extra question bank if needed.
- TLS, IPsec, SSH, VPN use cases
- picking the “best” control, not just a technically true one
- Keep one running sheet of acronyms and tricky pairs
- Start flashcards immediately for crypto and governance terms
- Keep an   error log   with 3 tags:
- Revisit only the weak objective tied to each miss
- Review all wrong answers and all lucky guesses
Practical Tactics for Crypto and Governance Weaknesses
Study crypto in comparison groups, not isolated definitions:
- Digital signature: supports   integrity, authenticity, non-repudiation
- Asymmetric: key exchange, signatures, cert-based trust
Use one-page comparison notes and repeat them every Saturday.
Memorize governance by role and purpose:
Then connect them to real scenarios:
- Aim for   80-85%   on mixed practice tests before exam day
- Don’t over-invest in memorizing every framework detail; focus on   what problem each control solves
- Flag long scenario questions and keep moving
